title: Mind the Gap: Attainable Data Movement and Operational Intensity Bounds for Tensor Algorithms
problem: Design-space exploration for tensor algorithms lacks tight bounds on data movement; the commonly used algorithmic minimum (compulsory misses) limit is extremely loose and fails to account for how buffers exploit reuse to reduce data movement.
motivation: Data movement is rapidly emerging as a critical metric for design-space exploration due to its increasing impact on both performance and energy efficiency.
method: Orojenesis computes attainable data movement bounds by accounting for buffer reuse across varying onchip storage capacities. The approach generates ski-slope diagrams that visualize the relationship between buffer size and minimum achievable data movement to each memory hierarchy level. It analyzes tensor algorithms including batched matrix multiplications, convolutions, and LLM operation sequences while accounting for operator fusion and producer-consumer reuse.
key_novelty: Computing attainable (reuse-aware) data movement bounds constrained by buffer capacity rather than just algorithmic minimum bounds, visualized through ski-slope diagrams.
contributions: Orojenesis framework for computing tight data movement bounds that comprehend buffer reuse and capacity constraints
Ski-slope diagrams providing interpretable insights into workload behavior as a function of storage capacity
Analysis revealing attainable data movement can be orders-of-magnitude higher than algorithmic minimum
Demonstration of 5.6x data movement reduction through operator fusion in GPT-3-6.7b with 320MB buffer

metrics.other: 5.6x data movement reduction with fusion (GPT-3-6.7b, 320MB buffer capacity)

limitations: Applicability to irregular tensor operations and sparse computation not discussed.
primary_theme: Tight data movement bounds for tensor algorithms
